source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
The CyrusOne San Antonio campus publishes 33 MW of IT capacity, placing it sixth among Texas facilities that disclose power figures and representing 6.9% of the state's disclosed 475 MW total.

At 40 kW per rack, this capacity would support roughly 825 racks suitable for AI training. At 100 kW per rack for GPU-dense inference, roughly 330 racks. The 175,000 square feet of technical space and power budget suggest a facility built for sustained high-density compute, though the operator does not specify whether current utilization or future planning targets AI workloads specifically.

The certifications—SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, and TIA-942—indicate this campus is architected for regulated enterprise and government workloads. These compliance frameworks matter for workloads where data residency or security clearance requirements are binding, not necessarily for AI scaling itself. The facility is designed for security-sensitive computing, not differentiated for compute intensity.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities but only 19 publish IT power figures. CyrusOne San Antonio is among the disclosed minority. This gap means the state's actual installed compute capacity remains largely unknown. For tracking how power and building constraint bind AI growth, facilities willing to publish capacity are few enough that each disclosed site becomes a marker of infrastructure willing to be transparent about its limits.
